title: Targeted NGS as follow-on DST
dek: Amplicon sequencing of resistance loci from sputum, without waiting for culture. Depth for heteroresistance; panels still live or die by WHO catalogue versioning.
story: Targeted NGS (tNGS) sequences a panel of resistance-associated genes/loci — typically rpoB (whole or RRDR+), katG, inhA, pncA, embB, gyrA/B, rrs/eis, Rv0678, atpE, rplC/rrl, ddn/fbi — directly from clinical specimens. WHO has a path for tNGS as a follow-on DST after RR-TB is found, and increasingly as a broader WRD class when products meet evaluation bars.

The selling point versus Xpert is breadth plus allele fraction. The selling point versus WGS-from-culture is time. The failure modes are amplicon dropout (lineage SNPs under primers), incomplete pncA/Rv0678 coverage, and calling phylogenetic SNPs as resistance.
A tNGS report that says “embB mutation detected” without the amino-acid change, grade, AF, and depth is not a result. Same discipline as WGS.
deep: Hotspot-only rpoB misses I491F. Full-gene pncA is not optional if you claim PZA. Full-gene Rv0678 if you claim BDQ.
Deeplex-MycTB and similar commercial panels are products; the catalogue is the grading layer. Version both.
5% AF at 2000× on an amplicon is a different object from 5% at 15× on WGS.
Mixed infection (two lineages) looks like heteroresistance until you look at unlinked SNPs.

visual.caption: From RR-TB WRD to a tNGS panel to graded alleles. Culture/WGS remain the residual and the relatedness tool.

example.title: Dropout of pncA amplicon
example.setup: tNGS calls FQ-S, INH-R (katG S315T), RIF-R (S450L). pncA: no coverage. Team writes PZA-S.

steps.title: No coverage is not wild type
steps.body: You cannot grade a gene you did not sequence.

steps.title: Reflex
steps.body: Repeat, different primers, or culture WGS. PZA in a 9-month regimen is not a guess.

steps.title: Report the gap
steps.body: “pncA failed” is a result. “PZA-S” is a fiction.

example.takeaway: tNGS is only as complete as the amplicons that actually sequenced.

choices: Amplicon sequencing of selected DR loci, often direct-from-specimen, graded by a catalogue
Proof that culture is obsolete for relatedness
check.answer: Amplicon sequencing of selected DR loci, often direct-from-specimen, graded by a catalogue

check.prompt: An rpoB S450L call at AF 0.06 with 1800× amplicon depth is:
choices: Indistinguishable from 2/20 WGS reads at codon 450
A better-supported minority than 2/20 WGS reads, but still a heteroresistance object to report with AF
check.answer: A better-supported minority than 2/20 WGS reads, but still a heteroresistance object to report with AF
check.why: Depth changes the binomial, not the clinical meaning of a minority.

whyWrong.Indistinguishable from 2/20 WGS reads at: Poisson error is not the same.

check.prompt: On the tNGS flow map, what does the “gaps” arrow to culture WGS represent?
choices: That tNGS already sequenced PE/PPE for clustering
That dropout, silent loci, mixed infection, and relatedness still need a genome-wide residual
check.answer: That dropout, silent loci, mixed infection, and relatedness still need a genome-wide residual
check.why: tNGS is follow-on DST, not a complete microbiology department.
